outcome.technical: drive-phase.py: (1) A redo no longer takes the old tree down. set_aside_tree (drive-phase.py:4842) rewrites the tree's marker to a keptTrees key '<id> set aside <n>' (so task-add never adopts it), records the key in keptTrees (which audit-status's kept_trees_block lists), renames the directory to '<tree>.aside-<n>' beside the task's path (:4880), then _repair_moved_tree runs `git worktree repair` and re-points each checked-out submodule's core.worktree under <admin>/modules. That is needed because `git worktree move` refuses a tree with a submodule checked out (observed: 'fatal: working trees containing submodules cannot be moved or removed'). On a failed rename it restores the marker and drops the key. recut_tree then cuts the new tree at the task's path as before. Once the recut holds the work, the set-aside tree goes to the remover with carried=<work commit>, and the redo's did-line says 'old tree set aside at X and removed' or 'old tree set aside at X, kept (why)'. drop_tree is deleted. (2) remove_task_tree (:4677) is now the ONLY place drive-phase force-removes a task tree (`git worktree remove --force`, :4726). It asks carry_commit, then the strict tree_undescribed, then carried-or-integrated (tree_holds_only_integrated, rewritten to read the work commit's paths so assume-unchanged edits are compared too), then that the phase head holds the tree's HEAD, that the marker names the task or set-aside key, and that cwd is not inside the tree. Any doubt returns (False, why) and the caller writes a did-line; it never stops the drive. Callers, with lines: retire_member :4754 (member tree), retire_asides :4797 (set-aside trees at retire), recut_tree :5837 (set-aside tree after the recut). No other task-tree remover remains in drive-phase: the remaining os.remove/rmtree sites (:3667 scratch index dir, :3710 phase-tree file revert, :5673 redo patch, :6432 state file, :6612 slice returns) are not trees. Removers outside this task, named and not edited: manage-worktrees.py:394 (`remove [--force]`) and :740 (`task-remove [--force]`); _worktrees.py:1035 (sweep's `worktree remove`), :1352 (sweep's `worktree prune`: it would delete a moved tree's admin dir and its submodule repos if it ran between set_aside_tree's rename and its repair), :1747 (_drop_copy, copies only). (3) The over-fires are relaxed. tree_undescribed(strict=False) on the redo now passes: an unchanged link that was never checked out (in either reading, as long as its directory is empty); a checked-out submodule at its recorded commit; and a staged state the disk has moved past (the path is also in the work's change against HEAD). A link whose commit differs between index/HEAD/work, or whose checkout HEAD differs, nested repos, unmerged paths, and non-superseded staged states still refuse the redo. strict=True (the remover) also names a checked-out submodule, a link directory holding files, any staged state, and a non-empty <admin>/modules. _unheld diffs with --ignore-submodules=dirty, and reports submodules with only their own dirt as 'left'. carry_commit then writes the commit and returns the left note in `why` (every caller reads `why` only when sha is None), and carry_work prints it on a did-line. (4) tree_undescribed's docstring now states that ignored files are not part of what it describes. Tests: a new STAGES row ta-block (_set_aside_cases, 14 cases, ~25 s alone). Updated in ar-block: ar18b (dirty ignore=dirty submodule now recuts, aside kept with the edit) and ar6d (now fails the set-aside rename instead of task-remove, and also asserts the marker is restored and no aside is recorded). ar18f is deleted (superseded by ta2).
